All consistent. Headline MAE numbers (4.7/6.2/8.0/5.5; saturated 8.2 vs 2.9; other 3.6 vs 7.3) recomputed from results.json and match. Unit/algorithm correct. evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 5 tests pass. Seeded 3 mutations in core logic, reverting each (git status clean afterwards): (M1) hold_printer adds only `load` instead of load+unload to printer demand (the one thing the project is about): all 5 tests PASSED, not caught; (M2) in mva.py the probability update ignores multi-server (`D/n` instead of `D/min(n,m)`): all 5 PASSED, not caught; (M3) sim.py failure probability halved: 1 test failed (caught, by the loose test_sim_below_held_capacity_at_saturation only by luck of the 10% slack). The tests are weak: no known-value MVA check beyond N=1, no comparison to a brute-force product-form solution, no regression on results.json, no test of the error-aggregation in run.py. Two of three core-logic mutants survive.
evidence.craft: Read mva.py, sim.py, run.py, test_held.py. Defects: (a) src is a byte-identical copy of robofab-cell-cv's package (diff -r empty), the third copy of the same engine in the research tree (cv, mva, held); (b) run.py builds the grid so that rows P=8/wip 4 duplicate P=4/wip 4 and P=16/wip 8 duplicate P=8/wip 8 exactly (same seeds, printer never binding): 4 of 32 rows are identical pairs, silently inflating the 'other rows' group and counted as independent; (c) no CI/standard errors or paired test on the error differences despite 20 seeds; (d) the saturated grouping is defined after seeing prior results (author admits) and wip=2P rows are 8 of 32; (e) mva() allocates O(K*N) arrays inside loops, fine at this size; (f) `pe` dict and `typ` dict never cleaned for pe (minor leak). Code is readable and commented, reproducible with fixed seeds, no silent fallbacks.
evidence.claims: Headline numbers all back to results.txt (verified). Overclaims found: README says plain MVA 'is already within a few percent' at low and moderate WIP, but on the 24 non-saturated rows 8 exceed 5% error for plain MVA, max 10.5% (P=4 wip 6, cv 1.0), and held MVA is better on two P+2 rows of P=4. After removing the 4 duplicated rows (28 unique), overall MAE is plain 4.9 vs held 5.6, other-rows 3.6 vs 6.7 (README: 4.7 vs 6.2, 3.6 vs 7.3): direction unchanged but the 32-row framing overstates the evidence. 'the grouping was chosen before the numbers were computed' is unverifiable. Limits and 'simulation-only, illustrative times' disclaimers are present and honest. Citations are not re-checked ('no web access'), refs.bib has 3 entries and Little (1961) is never cited in text. Does not cite the work that directly treats this problem (see fitness).
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: Jacobson and Lazowska 1982 (CACM, 'Analyzing queueing networks with simultaneous resource possession', surrogate-delay method) which is exactly a printer held while waiting for the arm; Akyildiz 1988 and Balsamo et al. on MVA for networks with blocking; Seidmann/Schweitzer/Shalev-Oren 1987 multiserver approximations; Marie 1979. None is cited or run as a baseline (README names Seidmann-style and Marie-type only as unbuilt next steps). The result, that adding the held time to demand fixes only bottleneck-saturated throughput (because the bound is capacity-driven there) and underestimates elsewhere (it omits that held time only occupies the printer when it is actually waiting for the arm), is sound but expected and well-known in the simultaneous-resource-possession literature; novelty is low and the contribution is a small negative result in a stylised model with illustrative parameters. A researcher could use the code and table as a worked example, but not as a basis for a publication without implementing a surrogate-delay baseline and measuring a real cell. One arm, one mix, two cv.
evidence.domain: A performance modeller would first ask why the naive repair was tried instead of the standard surrogate-delay iteration (Jacobson-Lazowska) that replaces the arm wait with an iterated printer-hold time; the held demand is the zero-wait limit of that scheme, so its behaviour (right at saturation, low otherwise) is predictable analytically. Departure from practice: no iteration on queueing delay, product-form MVA applied to a lognormal non-product-form system without discussion of insensitivity, utilisation bound compared as a 'predictor' although it is a bound, error reported as signed percent without intervals. Also the 'simulation as ground truth' is fine for the model but physical relevance (3D-print cell) is unstudied. Competent as a teaching experiment, below a publishable standard.

defects.what: Tests miss the central logic: seeded mutation dropping `unload` from the held printer demand and a mutation breaking multi-server MVA both pass all 5 tests; no brute-force MVA or results regression test.

Four of the 32 grid rows are exact duplicates (P=8 wip 4 = P=4 wip 4; P=16 wip 8 = P=8 wip 8, both cv values) and are counted as independent; deduped MAE is plain 4.9 vs held 5.6 overall, 3.6 vs 6.7 on other rows, differing from the published 4.7/6.2 and 7.3.

Does not cite or baseline against the directly relevant prior work (Jacobson-Lazowska simultaneous resource possession, MVA with blocking); the framing of the negative result as open is overstated, and 'next steps' name approximations that already exist.

defects.what: README says plain MVA is 'within a few percent' off saturation, but 8 of 24 such rows exceed 5% (max 10.5%).
src is a verbatim third copy of the cv package; refs.bib entry little1961 uncited; results.json float last-digit nondeterminism across runs.

verdict: The numbers are right: the experiment reproduces exactly, three MVA values (from a brute-force product-form solve) and four simulator rates (from an independently written DES) agree with the published table, and the headline means recompute. It is honest about being stylised and simulation-only. It does not meet the bar because verification is weak (two of three seeded core-logic mutants, including the project's own held-demand definition, pass all tests), four of 32 rows are duplicates counted as independent, one README sentence overstates plain MVA accuracy, and the work ignores the standard simultaneous-resource-possession literature that predicts the result, so novelty is low and it is a teaching-grade negative result rather than a publishable one.
